title: Descent of a counit-defined coefficient isomorphism through full embeddings
statement:
For $R=A,B$ let $\mathcal C_R,\mathcal D_R,\mathcal C'_R,\mathcal D'_R$ be categories (objects with Hom sets and associative unital composition), with functors $F_R:\mathcal C_R\to\mathcal D_R$, $I_R:\mathcal D_R\to\mathcal C_R$, $F'_R:\mathcal C'_R\to\mathcal D'_R$. Let $F_R\dashv I_R$ have counit $e_R$ [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection]. Let $S_{C,R}:\mathcal C_R\to\mathcal C'_R$ and $S_{D,R}:\mathcal D_R\to\mathcal D'_R$ be functors. Let coefficient functors be $T_C:\mathcal C_A\to\mathcal C_B$, $T_D:\mathcal D_A\to\mathcal D_B$, $T'_C:\mathcal C'_A\to\mathcal C'_B$, $T'_D:\mathcal D'_A\to\mathcal D'_B$, with natural isomorphisms $t_C:S_{C,B}T_C\xrightarrow{\sim}T'_CS_{C,A}$, $t_D:S_{D,B}T_D\xrightarrow{\sim}T'_DS_{D,A}$. Fix $M\in\mathcal D_A$, put $N=I_AM$ and $M_B=T_DM$. Let $\delta_{A,N}:S_{D,A}F_AN\to F'_AS_{C,A}N$ be a morphism. Let $\mathcal C^0_B\subseteq\mathcal C_B$ be a full subcategory containing $T_CN$ and $I_BM_B$, and let $\delta_{B,X}:S_{D,B}F_BX\to F'_BS_{C,B}X$ for $X\in\mathcal C^0_B$ be a family natural in $X\in\mathcal C^0_B$. Choose an object $Q_A\in\mathcal C'_A$. Let $\mathcal V_B$ be a full subcategory of $\mathcal D'_B$ containing $S_{D,B}M_B$ and $T'_DS_{D,A}M$, with their isomorphism $t_{D,M}$, and let $J_B:\mathcal V_B\to\mathcal C'_B$ be a functor. Suppose there are isomorphisms
$$\alpha_A:S_{C,A}N\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_A,\qquad
\alpha_B:S_{C,B}I_BM_B\xrightarrow{\sim}J_BS_{D,B}M_B,$$
and a family $E_{B,Q}:F'_BJ_BQ\to Q$, natural for the isomorphism $t_{D,M}:S_{D,B}M_B\to T'_DS_{D,A}M$, together with a morphism $E_A:F'_AQ_A\to S_{D,A}M$, such that
$$E_A F'_A(\alpha_A)\delta_{A,N}=S_{D,A}(e_{A,M}),\quad
E_{B,S_{D,B}M_B}F'_B(\alpha_B)\delta_{B,I_BM_B}=S_{D,B}(e_{B,M_B}).$$
Let $c:T_DF_AN\xrightarrow{\sim}F_BT_CN$ be an isomorphism, and let $c'_Q:T'_DF'_AQ\to F'_BT'_CQ$ be a family natural for $\alpha_A:S_{C,A}N\to Q_A$, with invertible components at those two objects. Assume
$$c'_{S_{C,A}N}T'_D(\delta_{A,N})t_{D,F_AN}
=F'_B(t_{C,N})\delta_{B,T_CN}S_{D,B}(c).$$
Suppose $b':T'_CQ_A\xrightarrow{\sim}J_BT'_DS_{D,A}M$ satisfies
$$E_{B,T'_DS_{D,A}M}F'_B(b')=T'_D(E_A)(c'_{Q_A})^{-1}.$$
Assume that $S_{C,B}$ is fully faithful on a full subcategory containing $T_CN$ and $I_BM_B$, that $S_{D,B}$ is injective on $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal D_B}(F_BT_CN,M_B)$, and that $\delta_{A,N},\delta_{B,T_CN},\delta_{B,I_BM_B}$ are isomorphisms. Then there is a unique isomorphism $b:T_CN\xrightarrow{\sim}I_BM_B$ whose image under $S_{C,B}$ is
$$(J_B(t_{D,M})\alpha_B)^{-1}\,b'\,(T'_C(\alpha_A)t_{C,N}).$$
It satisfies the original counit identity
$$e_{B,M_B}\circ F_B(b)=T_D(e_{A,M})\circ c^{-1}.$$
All displayed products are compositions with the rightmost factor applied first. No ambient exceptional functor or adjunction on all of $\mathcal D'_R$ is required: $Q_A$ is one object and $J_B$ is defined only on $\mathcal V_B$. The comparison $\delta$ is needed only at $N$ and on $\mathcal C^0_B$. Full faithfulness and faithfulness are needed only on the stated objects and Hom set; the coefficient functors need not preserve bounded-below objects globally.

proof.text: Use right-to-left composition as in the statement. Abbreviate $X=T_CN$, $Y=I_BM_B$, $U=S_{C,A}N$, $Q=Q_A$, $W=S_{D,B}M_B$, $Z=T'_DS_{D,A}M$, $S=S_{D,B}$, $H=F'_B$, $t=t_{D,M}$, $a=\alpha_A$, $a_B=\alpha_B$, $d_X=\delta_{B,X}$, $d_Y=\delta_{B,Y}$ and $d_A=\delta_{A,N}$. Set $u=T'_C(a)t_{C,N}$ and $v=J_B(t)a_B$. Functors carry an inverse to the inverse of the image, by applying them to the two inverse identities. Thus $u$ and $v$ are isomorphisms, and $h=v^{-1}b'u:S_{C,B}X\to S_{C,B}Y$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Proof, closed-immersion counit descent; explicit elementary calculation extracted from the retained proof of lem-coef-finite-dualizing

proof.text: Full faithfulness on the stated full subcategory means bijectivity on its Hom sets. Lift $h$ and $h^{-1}$ to $b:X\to Y$ and $g:Y\to X$. The images of $gb$ and $bg$ are respectively $h^{-1}h=1$ and $hh^{-1}=1$. Injectivity on the endomorphism sets of $X,Y$ gives $gb=1_X$ and $bg=1_Y$, so $b$ is an isomorphism. Injectivity on $\operatorname{Hom}(X,Y)$ makes it the unique morphism with the required image. The subcategory used here need not equal $\mathcal C_B^0$: both contain $X,Y$ and are full.

source.place: Proof, closed-immersion counit descent; explicit elementary calculation extracted from the retained proof of lem-coef-finite-dualizing

proof.text:
Since $X,Y\in\mathcal C_B^0$ and this subcategory is full, $b$ is a morphism to which the assumed naturality of $\delta_B$ applies. It gives $d_Y S(F_B(b))=H(S_{C,B}(b))d_X$. Define $L=S(e_{B,M_B})S(F_B(b))S(c)$. Substitute the given $B$-counit identity $S(e_{B,M_B})=E_{B,W}H(a_B)d_Y$ and then the naturality equation to obtain
$$L=E_{B,W}H(a_BS_{C,B}(b))d_XS(c).$$
All these maps have source $ST_DF_AN$ and target $W$.

source.place: Proof, closed-immersion counit descent; explicit elementary calculation extracted from the retained proof of lem-coef-finite-dualizing

proof.text:
The defining image $S_{C,B}(b)=v^{-1}b'u$ gives $a_BS_{C,B}(b)=J_B(t)^{-1}b'T'_C(a)t_{C,N}$. Naturality of $E_B$ at the given isomorphism $t:W\to Z$ reads $tE_{B,W}=E_{B,Z}H(J_B(t))$, and hence $E_{B,W}H(J_B(t)^{-1})=t^{-1}E_{B,Z}$. Substituting these two equalities and functoriality into the preceding expression yields
$$L=t^{-1}E_{B,Z}H(b')H(T'_C(a))H(t_{C,N})d_XS(c).$$
Only objects $W,Z$ and their isomorphism in $\mathcal V_B$ are used.

source.place: Proof, closed-immersion counit descent; explicit elementary calculation extracted from the retained proof of lem-coef-finite-dualizing

proof.text:
The assumed coefficient square is exactly $H(t_{C,N})d_XS(c)=c'_U T'_D(d_A)t_{D,F_AN}$. The defining counit equation for $b'$ is $E_{B,Z}H(b')=T'_D(E_A)(c'_Q)^{-1}$. Substituting these equalities gives
$$L=t^{-1}T'_D(E_A)(c'_Q)^{-1}H(T'_C(a))c'_U T'_D(d_A)t_{D,F_AN}.$$

source.place: Proof, closed-immersion counit descent; explicit elementary calculation extracted from the retained proof of lem-coef-finite-dualizing

proof.text:
The specified naturality of $c'$ at $a:U\to Q$ reads
$$H(T'_C(a))c'_U=c'_Q T'_D(F'_A(a)).$$
Multiplying on the left by $(c'_Q)^{-1}$ cancels this component, so the previous equality becomes
$$L=t^{-1}T'_D(E_A F'_A(a)d_A)t_{D,F_AN}.$$
This uses only naturality along $a$ and invertibility of the stated component at $Q$; there is no extension of $c'$ to additional objects.

source.place: Proof, closed-immersion counit descent; explicit elementary calculation extracted from the retained proof of lem-coef-finite-dualizing

proof.text:
The given $A$-counit identity replaces $E_AF'_A(a)d_A$ by $S_{D,A}(e_{A,M})$. Naturality of $t_D$ for the morphism $e_{A,M}:F_AN\to M$ says
$$T'_D(S_{D,A}(e_{A,M}))t_{D,F_AN}=tS(T_D(e_{A,M})).$$
Thus the previous equality simplifies by $t^{-1}t=1$ to $L=S(T_D(e_{A,M}))$.

source.place: Proof, closed-immersion counit descent; explicit elementary calculation extracted from the retained proof of lem-coef-finite-dualizing

proof.text:
Expand $L$ and precompose the equality of the preceding step with $S(c^{-1})$. Functoriality and $cc^{-1}=1$ give
$$S(e_{B,M_B}\circ F_B(b))=S(T_D(e_{A,M})\circ c^{-1}).$$
Both preimages are morphisms in $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal D_B}(F_BX,M_B)$, exactly the Hom set on which $S$ is assumed injective. Injectivity therefore proves the claimed original counit identity. Existence and uniqueness of the required isomorphism were proved above. No global right adjoint in a primed category, no naturality of $\delta_A$ away from $N$, and no preservation of an ambient subcategory by a coefficient functor enter the calculation.
